title: Dispatch one typed Client display-name replacement

requirements.invariant: Renaming a Client is one distinct RenameClient outcome over stable AccountID and ClientID. The current name is mutable display text, never identity, relationship or Transfer authority, and the rename changes no other Client responsibility.

RenameClient changes only the current Client display value. Current Project display later resolves by stable ClientID, while frozen Invoice, report, paid-history and audit snapshots remain unchanged; the use case cannot change Project ownership or authorize Transfer from name equality.

RenameClient is distinct from CreateClient, ArchiveClient, ChangeProjectClient and MergeClients. The use case carries no lifecycle, child, accounting, history, merge, alias or reassignment input, so O-024/O-025 remain open and unchanged.

ClientRenameIntent is a transient, non-Codable, exact Account/Client/revision/ClientDisplayName presentation value. It owns no raw field, alternate validator, persisted form draft, initial/current read, readiness, lifecycle, dirty/no-op, dismissal, error-UX, route, provider identity or authorization claim.

ClientRenameUseCase constructs the verified ClientRenameDraft and RenameClientCommand before invoking ClientRenaming.rename exactly once, then validates and returns the exact receipt and LocalOperationState.

The use case preserves CancellationError and every ClientRenameFailure. Only an unknown port error maps to localAcceptanceFailed; construction remains outside the port catch and receipt validation remains outside it.

Only the two new target leaves advance. ClientRenameOperation/tests, ClientProjectDirectory/tests and ClientCoreDetailsData/tests stay verified; EditProjectModal, ProjectDetailView, ProjectDetailContainer, ProjectService/Protocol, Project model, ProjectFormValidation/tests, the projects MCP module and update_project retain their prior status and content because each owns broader responsibility.

Exactly two target-only executable leaves may change after READY. Physical persistence, optimistic projection, trusted authorization/audit/apply, Postgres/Data API/RLS/PowerSync/provider behavior, app/MCP wiring, source migration, hosted resources, production, release and cutover do not advance.

Verified dependency evidence EVID-CLIENT-RENAME-001 remains sole owner of accepted ClientDisplayName bytes, ExpectedClientRevision, the exact same-Client revision precondition, ClientRenameDraft, RenameClientCommand, subject, fingerprint, receipt validation and ClientRenameFailure semantics. This use case consumes the already-validated name and composes those contracts without raw String normalization or semantic reimplementation.

items: ClientRenameIntent is transient, non-Codable and exposes an exact public four-argument initializer for AccountID, ClientID, ExpectedClientRevision and ClientDisplayName.
The use case reuses ClientRenameDraft and RenameClientCommand and accepts no raw String or alternate normalization rule.
Construction finishes before one ClientRenaming.rename call; receipt validation follows the port boundary; all 12 typed failures and cancellation remain exact while unknown errors are bounded.
No initial/current read, readiness, lifecycle, dirty/no-op, UI, Client correction or Project ownership policy is added.

The deterministic in-memory test port cannot physically persist, authorize, synchronize, deploy, display, migrate, release or cut over a Client rename.

verification.expected: A non-@testable consumer constructs the exact public four-field ClientRenameIntent. It is compile-time Equatable/Sendable, runtime non-Codable, stores no raw String, and preserves zero and UInt64.max revisions exactly.

An already-validated ClientDisplayName, including accepted outer/interior whitespace and more than 8 KiB Unicode, reaches draft and payload byte-exactly after one call; the use case accepts no raw String and performs no second normalization.

Every LocalOperationState returns in the exact validated receipt after exactly one call carrying one Client rename and one same-Client expected-revision precondition; revisions zero and UInt64.max dispatch exactly.

A reciprocal flattened encoded-leaf matrix independently varies Account, Client, revision, typed display name, Operation, actor, contract and time against literal flattened baseline expectations and exact literal changed-leaf sets for all eight axes. Recording/canned fakes and expectation helpers must not reconstruct expected commands with ClientRenameDraft, RenameClientCommand or production validation logic.
Positive infinity and NaN capture times fail during construction with zero calls, while a mismatched receipt fails after exactly one call; neither is reclassified as a port failure.

All 12 ClientRenameFailure values deliberately thrown by the port remain exact after one call, CancellationError remains structured cancellation, and only an unknown port error maps to localAcceptanceFailed.
All 12 diagnostic codes remain an exact stable enumeration and reveal no synthetic identity, Client name, raw error, credential, service payload or production identifier.

Exact nested command topology exposes only draft/envelope/subject/fingerprint ownership, typed replacement display name and one expected-revision precondition—never raw-name, Project ownership/reassignment, lifecycle, archive/delete/merge/alias, accounting, frozen history, UI or service detail.
